gaps.what: The regenerated RI-CMB07 exemplar is a 120-second, 7200-frame fight in which the player is never hit. Eleven of twenty-four banded rows are out of band against RI-CMB07 M2's floor of at most four, over one fight against a floor of five. Of the enemy's 26 swings, 11.5% were dodged and 7.7% blocked; the other 81% simply missed.

gaps.what: The entire Writ House creation sequence renders nothing. Driving all 19 census nodes through window.__HARNESS and screenshotting after each at 1920x1080 produces 20 byte-identical PNGs (sha256 7277a273453ac8631c318f3d9120d7b12b7f562b187adabf59fe3ca7b5daaeb5) showing a body standing in an empty green field: no barge hold, no Writ House interior, no Jeeh-Ei, no Warden-Scribe Tuleeh-Ma, no question, no answer options, and document.body.innerText empty at every node. listEntities() returns 0 entities before and after creation. The scene exists only as a JSON state machine whose getCensusState() self-reports full_screen:false, world_visible:true and full_screen_panels:0 — three fields with no rendered counterpart. RI-CHR01's first bar is 'creation is a scene, not a screen'; what shipped is neither, and RI-JRN01's whole Diegesis block (35 of its 100 points) has nothing to measure.

From the player's chair crime has no consequence, which is the exact failure RI-CRM01 exists to prevent and the exact shape RI-MTH07 warns about one level up: the model is computed, consumed, and then thrown away by the interaction that resolves it. gaps.what: An enemy attack's swept volume does not cover the attacker's own root translation, so it cannot hit a target standing inside its forward root travel. Measured on a stationary player against a stationary champion_hist_marked in arena_champion, sweeping 0.0-4.0 m in 0.1 m steps: the chop hits from 1.2 m to 3.6 m and misses at EVERY distance from 0.0 to 1.1 m; the thrust hits 1.6-4.0 m and misses 0.0-1.5 m; combo_a hits 1.1-2.9 m and misses 0.0-1.0 m. Those minimum distances are the attacks' declared root_dz_m of 1.2 / 1.6 / 0.9. Zeroing root_dz_m moves the inner boundary to 0.6 / 0.8 / 0.8 m, confirming the root translation is the cause (data file reverted, git clean). The player's own weapons have no such hole — dagger, straight sword, spear, greatsword and halberd all hit from 0.0 m. The consequence, measured: a player who stands completely still at 0.8-1.1 m and does nothing but mash the light attack kills the 2876-HP champion in 1153-1377 frames taking ZERO damage, while the enemy completes 44-54 frames of live hitbox and suffers zero stagger frames. This is also the mechanical cause of the exemplar's headline out-of-band row: 141 of 211 enemy swings resolve as WHIFF, and 35 swings across five fights had the player invulnerable for every active frame at 0.01-0.60 m — inside the hole, where the swing could not have connected anyway, so i-frame negation reads 0.111 against a band of 0.40-0.80.
gaps.why_it_matters: The correct way to fight this game's boss is to walk inside it and stand still, which makes rolling, spacing, stamina and the entire i-frame system that RI-CMB01 gets exactly right decorative.

remedy.action: Sweep the attacker's root translation as well as its animated pose. RI-CMB04 §A's step order runs 5 (consume root motion) before 8 (sweep + query, this frame's pose vs last frame's); the sweep must interpolate the weapon socket capsule between last frame's WORLD-space pose and this frame's WORLD-space pose — root delta included — and the SUBSTEPS count must be derived from the larger of the arc travel and the root travel, not from the arc alone. A root_dz_m of 1.2 m spread over a 10-frame active window is 0.12 m per frame, which is inside one capsule radius, so the fix is a space change rather than a substep increase; verify both. Then re-derive SUBSTEPS from the measured maximum of (per-frame tip travel, per-frame root travel).

gaps.what: The round-2 hole in the weapon volume is untouched; it has been covered by a second volume that pays the weapon's damage. Ablation, measured on a copy of the loaded data with no file edited: delete `hitgeometry.json §body_hazard` and the champion's minimum reaching distance against a stationary player returns to chop 1.2 m, thrust 1.6 m, combo_a 1.1 m, combo_b 1.2 m — round 2's numbers to the decimal. With the block present, every hit inside those radii carries `via: "body"`, and a body hit deals the attack's full weapon damage: chop 96 at 0.05 m via body is the same 96 as at 3.65 m via weapon, thrust 75, combo_a 63. It is the same on the player's side — the dagger's blade cannot cut inside 0.75 m and the straight sword's inside 0.80 m, so 14 of the dagger's 19 connecting distances and 15 of the straight sword's 36 are torso-checks. Two of the seven player classes fail S26's contiguity clause outright, and the gaps sit exactly at the seam between the two volumes: the spear's body corridor stops at 1.15 m and its blade starts at 1.30 m, leaving 1.20-1.25 m dead; the halberd's stops at 1.10 m and starts at 1.35 m, leaving 1.15-1.30 m dead. Reproduced identically in headless Chromium and in the node arena. And it is what the fight is made of: in the shipping game, 5 to 7 of the 8 blows that kill a motionless player are `via: body`.
gaps.why_it_matters: A player who walks inside the champion watches a 1.75 m greatsword sweep over their head and loses 96 hit points to the chest that walked through them, and a spearman standing at 1.22 m cannot be hit by anything at all.

remedy.action: Two changes, in this order. (1) Fix the weapon volume rather than compensating for it. At the champion's first active frame the chop's socket capsule spans z = [1.34, 2.57] with the root at z = 0.384, i.e. the blade's near end is 0.95 m in front of its own root and never re-enters the 0.4-1.1 m band. Give the enemy archetypes' `chop_overhead` and `thrust` clip archetypes in game/data/combat/clips.json a low phase — a follow-through that brings the guard socket down through the attacker's own front quarter — so the swept hull covers the band the attacker is walking through. The gate at game/src/engine.js:2011 is `!!(this.hearths && this.hearths.atHearth && this.hearths.atHearth(this.sim)) || !!this.sim._uiForceHearth`, and HearthSystem (game/src/sim/hearth.js) defines list/get/count/nearest/at/gateAt/menu and no `atHearth`. gaps.why_it_matters: The player banks souls, risks them, dies, walks back and recovers exactly 4,200 of them — and then cannot spend one, which makes the entire death economy this piece implements so carefully a loop with nothing at the end of it.

gaps.what: RI-JRN03's entire 'Discoverability without instruction' block — 14 of its 100 points, and the home of hard fail HF5 — is unmeasured, and the one check in it that reports a result reports it from an empty buffer. M-K20 searches window.__HARNESS.getRenderedText() for instruction tokens and passed with `frames: 0`. I drove the register in seven named states (arena_flat, helstrom-market, thorn-hall, ui-journal, npc_showcase, default, settlement_primary_street) and through uiOpen('dialogue'), uiOpen('menu') and uiOpen('rest'): entries = 0 and summary.surfaces = {} in every single one, while getUIState() at the same instant reports three HUD elements carrying drawn text ('5', 'LIGHT', 'Spark-Dart'). game/src/render/text-register.js instruments only the 'dialogue' and 'title' surfaces and neither ever writes. M-K21 and M-K22 — the other 8 points of the block, M-K22 being the second half of HF5 — do not exist in tools/journey/input-checks.mjs at all; nor do M-K8 (HF3), M-K9 (HF4), M-N1/M-N2/M-N3/M-N5(HF10)/M-N7, M-P14, M-P20, M-P24 (HF7) or M-P25. gaps.what: 37,819 words in 65 texts open 65/65 in the engine across 324 pages, and the only thing a player can do with any of it is read it. Both mechanical consumers the two items name are dead code. (1) `book.knowledge_key` is read by no file in game/src/; the three non-violent quest resolutions that gate on those keys — Q-SOUL-02 res_seal, Q-LILM-01 res_rootkeepers, Q-DEEP-01 res_broker — are unreachable by any route in the shipped build, and the engine reports the identical refusal before and after the book has been opened and read to the last page. (2) `book.topics_taught` (60 books, 116 topics) is read by nothing; opening all 60 in the engine leaves topicsKnown empty. That field is RI-UIX05 R3's permitted exception and the item's entire declared AR-3 seam crossing.
gaps.why_it_matters: RI-UIX05 §D's last row exists, in the item's own words, because 'a player who read the right book three regions ago knows a name, and a name is a parley key (S13) or a topic (R3's exception) ... this row owns whether the reading surface is connected to anything.' It reports 17 by reading JSON and 0 by asking the game. Three of the build's non-violent exits are closed, which pushes against the >=45% non-combat resolution bar; and the piece's only route across the Souls/Morrowind seam does not exist. ARBITRATION §3 CONSUMPTION is explicit that a model with no demonstrated consumer scores 0 exactly as a missing model does, because from the player's chair they are the same thing.

gaps.what: A spell does not connect with anything that moves. A LIGHT-class bolt fired at a body 18 m away deals 80 damage when the body is stationary and 0 damage the moment it moves laterally at 1.5 m/s - slower than the walk speed measured in the same arena, 3.17 m/s - and 0 at 3, 5 and 7 m/s. spell_impact fires in every row; effect_apply fires only at 0 m/s. This is not the tracking fence: AP-M3 passes cleanly under an instrument that re-derives the turn rate from consecutive headings (LIGHT 60.00 dps before the fence and 0.00 after, 0 violating frames, --break=nocutoff red at 72 frames), and the arc is real at 21.95 deg on LIGHT and 24.16 deg on HEAVY. The bolt steers and still misses, because it steers toward the position it acquired at release rather than the position the target now occupies, and the 0.35 x journey fence closes before the error is paid off. The comparison that rules out an instrument artefact is touch range, measured the same way with the same setEntityPos calls: a retreating body takes full damage at 0 and 1 m/s and none at 3, so the harness demonstrably drives the same resolver.
gaps.why_it_matters: Every enemy in this build repositions - the arena's own bodies sit in REPOSITION for the whole of a 900-frame observation - so the offensive half of the catalogue, which is every projectile- and target-range effect and therefore all five damage effects and most of the status verbs, does not work against a live opponent at all. It also explains a structural fact about every census this piece has ever run, mine included: they all pin a body at 1.4 m and use touch range, because that is the only geometry that connects. DISTINCT-VERBS 53/55 is a true statement about a build in which the thing a player actually does with a spell in a fight does not land. And it is the round's own new protocol rule - if the thing being measured responds to motion, the target must move - applied to the one place the round that wrote it did not apply it.

gaps.what: The effect catalogue is a complete, correctly priced, deterministic parameter space with one behaviour behind it. Measured across all 71 shipped spells: 5 of 55 effects produce the mechanical consequence their own record describes (fire, frost, shock and poison damage, and damage_health); 1 is partial (levitate meters altitude and charges 1.5 Focus/m but never moves pos[1]); 16 resolve only as HP damage equal to their own magnitude — demoralise deals 111 hp and the enemy stays AGGRO, calm_beast deals 31 hp and the beast stays in COMBAT, open_lock deals 31 hp to a creature, charm 184, corrode 310, lock_lock 184, silence 31, paralyse 12 with no buildup field on the enemy record at all; and 33 are a row in effects_active that no other system in the build reads — shield and resist_element each mitigate 0 of a scripted 100-damage hit, the_greater_mending heals 0 with the player at 420 of 620, feather leaves equip_load_pct at 24 and roll_class at LIGHT, fortify_skill satisfies no gate, bind_lesser summons nothing (entity count 0 to 0), wall creates no collider, leap adds 0 m of altitude, recall completes its 210-frame ritual and leaves the player at exactly the coordinates it started from, hist_sight completes and writes 0 journal entries, and all five Veiling effects leave getStealthState() byte-identical to baseline against the stealth system shipping in the same build.
gaps.why_it_matters: S19 says spell effects are tools and quests must be solvable with them, so a player who buys the Open spell to get past the warded door in The Warded Ledger will instead do thirty-one points of damage to the door's guard, and the >=45% non-combat resolution bar that magic is supposed to supply a fifth of is satisfied only in JSON.

remedy.action: Replace the single generic applicator with a per-effect handler registry. Concretely: (1) In game/src/sim/combat-bridge.js, the spell-contact callback currently accumulates `dmg += outputOf(effect, magnitude)` for every effect whose utility_class is null OR whose geometry is not 'none' — restrict that accumulation to the five damage effects (fire_damage, frost_damage, shock_damage, poison_damage, damage_health) plus the status buildup each declares, so a non-damage effect can never deal HP damage. (2) Add game/src/sim/magic/apply.js: a table keyed by effect id, one handler per effect, called from MagicSystem.applyEffects(), each handler writing into the system RI-MAG06 §B names for that effect. (3) Wire the eight consumers that already exist in this build before touching anything that does not: CombatBody.equipLoadPct/tier for feather and burden (RI-CMB01's 30.00/70.00 cliff must stay exactly where it is); CombatBody.hp for restore_health, drain_health and absorb_health, and hpMax for drain; a mitigation multiplier ahead of the damage write for shield, resist_element and sap_ward; sim.stealth.d.detection's V terms and sound radius for chameleon (clamped 80), invisibility (breaking on attack, cast, interact, container and COMBAT), muffle, night_eye and false_face; the S11 buildup meter for paralyse, so it crosses a threshold instead of arriving in one frame; enemy alert_state and the leash for calm_beast, demoralise and frenzy, ending COMBAT with zero death events; CombatBody.pos for mark/recall/intervention, so a completed ritual actually moves the player; and a real locomotion mode for levitate that writes pos[1], caps horizontal speed at 1.4 m/s and drops light, heavy, block, roll and parry. (4) Every effect whose consuming system genuinely does not exist yet (water bands, the lock register, item condition, the quest knowledge store) gets an explicit UNMEASURABLE row in the census naming the piece that owns it, capped at five per RI-MAG06 M6.

gaps.what: MagicSystem.skills is a private object initialised to {sorcery:30, root_speech:30, warding:30, veiling:30} that no gameplay path writes. Measured in four shipped states (default, arena_flat, dungeon_primary, helstrom-market): 47 of 72 shipped spells attunable and 25 refused — all 17 tier-3 and all 8 tier-4 — and setAttuned() drops them silently. 40 casts at a live target, a HEARTH rest, H.setSkills() on the character sheet and H.grantSkillUse('cast_effective') all leave the tier-3 attune at 0/1 and quoteSpell().attunable_now false; only H.setMagicSkills(), a harness call with no in-game counterpart, flips it to 1/1 and true. In the other direction, RI-MAG04's magic resolutions gate on sim.progression.skills, which is {} in every shipped state and which the magic system never writes: the coupling between the character's magic skill and the magic system is 0.00 in both directions, with the null control clean (perturbing magic.skills 30->100 does flip the gate, so the probe is driving a live gate and not a stub).
gaps.why_it_matters: A mage who plays this game for forty hours casts exactly the spells they could cast in the first minute — a third of the shipped catalogue, every tier-3 and tier-4 spell, and every three-effect spell they might commission are locked behind a number that nothing they do can move, and the quest resolutions magic exists to unlock read a different, empty number.

gaps.what: RI-CHR01 §4 states the questionnaire's purpose in its own words — the Warden-Scribe says the profession aloud, 'which is the moment the route is for' — and RI-JRN09 M3 requires that line on the frame in 100% of named runs. Measured at the node the line is spoken (writ.birthsign, its only opportunity, because `spoken` carries only the reply to the last answer): 0 of 12 named runs across six races and two upbringings. The mechanism is ui.js's overflow-sacrifice loop — `while (contentH > maxH && spokenLines.length) spokenLines.shift()` — which drops the scribe's previous reply from the front until the panel fits its 48%-of-frame-height budget, and at the birthsign node (nine options plus a two-line naming sentence) the naming line is always what goes. The builder's own instrument reports 100% because it does not test that line: jrn09-exchange.mjs M3 runs `blob.indexOf(norm(c.class_name)) >= 0` over the concatenated drawn text of every node in the walk, and the same round added 'Trade declared: %ClassName' to the writ's drawn identity block at writ.stamp, so the class name is on the frame whatever the scribe did or did not say. Measured side by side on the same twelve runs: the naming LINE 0 of 12; the class NAME substring 12 of 12. The same mechanism eats the upbringing reply ('The interior. I will write the marsh. There are people here who will read that and stand up straighter, and people who will read it and count their doors.') and the birthsign reply ('The tide was in and the root had more than it needed. It gave you a swallow it did not owe you.'), which is why AC = 6 of 7 is evidenced entirely by fields of one printed form.
gaps.why_it_matters: Morrowind's opening is remembered because a bored functionary looks at your answers and tells you what you apparently are. This build computes that sentence, writes it, carries it through the model, exposes it through the harness — and clips it off the bottom of the panel, then prints the word on a form two nodes later. A player answers ten questions about wounded dogs and toll-houses and is never told anything; they later find a noun on a document. Round 3 closed round 2's orphan-text defect on the questions and opened the same defect on the answer, and the round's own instrument certified it closed. That is the third time in this project a measurement has passed because it tested something adjacent to what the item asked for, and it is the exact failure BAR-CRITIQUE-W1-07-R1 filed RI-JRN09 to prevent.

gaps.what: The moveset animation model — 1150 distinct clips over 2689 slots and 87 weapons, the solved arcs, the solved blade lengths, the 25-slot contract — has no renderer. `grep -rn "weapon" game/src/render/` returns nothing, `grep -rn "bone" game/src/render/` returns nothing, and no SkinnedMesh is constructed anywhere in game/src. `game/src/render/scene.js` makeActor() builds a rigid group of nine primitives — torso, head, snout, hips, two static legs, two static arms — plus `new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.055, 0.95, 0.014)` welded at local (0.40, 1.28, 0.10) as 'the blade', one 0.95 m box for all eighty-seven weapons. `game/src/render/renderer.js:398-399` is the whole of the player's animation: playerMesh.position.set(sim.player.pos) and playerMesh.rotation.y = yaw. Measured in the shipping build: across a full 60-frame r1.1, the character-box pixel change is 0.19% peak for hlb_garrison_bill (2.85 m, a 146.8 deg sweep over 14 active frames) and 0.21% for cgs_drowned_reaper (a `spin` over 18 active frames); ssw_garrison_sword's 2.4% is flat from f030 to f060 and is the root lunge translating a rigid mesh, not a swing. Frame-0 screenshots of ssw_garrison_sword (1.95 m), hlb_garrison_bill (2.85 m) and cgs_drowned_reaper (2.75 m) are byte-identical, md5 9bdb823fbcdb3ba820b2946b05ffa55a.
gaps.why_it_matters: WEAPON-CRITIC 0 states this role's whole subject: 'the deficit lives entirely in the animation-clip column of the moveset data and in the root tracks the clips produce.' ARBITRATION 3's CONSUMPTION check states the consequence: 'a model with no demonstrated consumer is unmeasurable => 0, exactly as a missing model is — from the player's chair they are the same thing', and it lists 'character creation rendered 20 byte-identical screenshots while returning correct values' as one of the four wave-1 instances. This is that instance again, in the area the check was written for. Round 1 found the 87 movesets unreachable from the running game; round 3 made them reachable to the hitbox solver; they are still unreachable to the screen. The builder demonstrated a consumer for the IMPACT model, correctly and convincingly, and never asked the same question of the ANIMATION model — whose only consumer is the solver that grades it. It is also the mechanism by which every other defect here survived three rounds: the blade points 35-52 degrees into the ground and sits 100% below the floor plane through the entire damaging window of CGS, HLB, TSW and WHP (so a halberd lands nothing at 2.65 m and nothing at all against a retreating target), and that is invisible to a critic who cannot see the swing and unmissable to anyone who can. The builder named the blade inclination as its own biggest remaining defect; this is the reason it was still there to name.

gaps.what: The RI-WPN05 impact and material model is a data island, exactly as the 87 movesets were in round 1. Five of six perturbations of the shipped tables change nothing in the fight: setting every non-flesh cell of the 5x7 attacker hitstop grid to 99 f, setting every material damage multiplier to 0.01, setting every knockback value to 9 m, and setting the deflection multiplier to 20x all produce a byte-identical fight (dmg 118, hit at frame 32, hitstop held 3 frames). Only the flesh column is read, and it is read from a hard-coded `.flesh` lookup at game/src/combat/moves.js:166. MovesetLibrary.materialMultiplier, .deflects, .knockbackFor and .victimHitstopFor are imported by exactly one file in the repository — game/src/harness/weapons.js, the harness. And there is nothing for them to apply to: 0 of the 14 enemy statblocks in game/data/combat/enemies/ declares a material at all. The hard-coded lookup is game/src/combat/moves.js:166 — `hitstop_frames: (s.hitstop_f || lib.classes.hitstop.attacker[moveset.weight_tier] || {}).flesh || 6` — and a grep for materialMultiplier|deflects|knockbackFor|victimHitstopFor across game/src/ returns only game/src/harness/weapons.js.
gaps.why_it_matters: This is round 1's verdict repeating itself one layer down, and it is invisible for the same reason: the builder fixed the half of the piece the round-1 gap named and the impact half was never examined, so every probe that reads the library reports a healthy 5x7 grid. From the player's chair a mace, an axe and a spear hit a stone golem, a chitin-shelled beast and a Hist-bonded plant creature with identical feedback — same hitstop, same knockback, no deflection, no damage-type advantage. The material system is also this area's ONLY seam crossing under AR-3: a lore fact (root-golems are stone, the Hist-bonded are plant) that is supposed to be a combat answer a merchant can sell you. Unread, the crossing does not exist, and the weapon area becomes internally excellent and externally sterile.

gaps.what: All thirteen regions are the same three primitives — canopy, under, rock — recoloured, and not one of the thirteen declared ONLY-HERE elements exists in the world. Every region in game/data/world/regions.json carries the identical prop schema `canopy+under+rock`, drawing on seven shared canopy shapes and five shared under shapes; the whole 14.31 km2 province renders with textureMB 0, atlasCount 0, 17 materials and 8 programs. `only_here: {id, instances}` — welkynd_pillar x34, petrified_bole x400, rock_flute_spire x14, glassed_crater x16, beached_hull_house x12 and nine more — is an integer literal in tools/world/build-regions.mjs and nothing places an instance, so RI-WLD04 M19 measures 0 of 13. Five of M18's nine axes (fauna, architecture, audio, weather, hazard) are DROPPED rather than measured, which is the same statement in the instrument's own words. The consequence is measurable two ways. A human taking M17 on the now-honest pack scores 4/8 against a pass bar of 85%, and three of the four misses are one miss: frames 023, 042 and 050 are the Stone Wastes — 'glassed salt crust', glass_thorn, whale_bone_frame, salt_block_wall, crater_rim — and all three read as Marauder's Coast, because what is rendered is a khaki flat under a white fog band. And with colour and exposure removed from the machine descriptor, leave-one-out identification falls 74.4% -> 30.8% and Fisher 3.10 -> 1.77: about two-thirds of the measured region separability is carried by tint alone, which is RI-WLD04's own named way to lose.
gaps.why_it_matters: S24 rules that thirteen regions must each read as a different place and that an implementation where everything is one terrain with a recoloured fog has failed regardless of how good the terrain is — and a player walking the 6.6 km crossing passes through five regions that differ in ground colour and in nothing they can name.

remedy.action: Place the ONLY-HERE elements as real instances, and give each region at least one prop class that no other region has. Concretely: (1) extend the region prop schema in tools/world/build-regions.mjs and game/src/world/province.js beyond `canopy+under+rock` with a fourth slot `signature`, carrying its own mesh generator per region — a welkynd pillar for Blackwood, a rock-flute spire for Valus Ridge, a whale-bone frame and crater rim for the Stone Wastes, a beached hull house and tide pole for Marauder's Coast, a drowned xanmeer tooth and corpse lily for the Deep Marshes, a stilt row and tideway marker for the Eastern Rootlands; (2) place them at the counts regions.json already declares, from the same seeded lattice the existing props use, so the number in the table becomes the number in the world; (3) add a `signature_silhouette` axis and an `architecture_placed` axis to tools/world/region-axes.mjs, computed from placed instances rather than from a table row, and un-drop `architecture`; (4) give the ground more than one material — at present textureMB is 0, so albedo is a per-region constant and RI-WLD04's 'albedo must come from different materials, not a LUT' cannot be satisfied at all.

gaps.what: The trunk road network is routed along the floors of water bodies. Sampling getWaterAt() at every point of all ten built legs at tide LOW: 1,364 m of road (5.4%) is above knee depth and 574 m (2.3%) is above chest depth, concentrated on the Stormhold-Helstrom leg, which carries 538 m over-knee and 502 m over-chest and reaches a maximum depth of 65.64 m at (2182.52, 2214.63) - ground at 69.66 m under a water surface at 135.30 m. That leg is the first of THE CROSSING, so 502 m of the canonical 6,788 m walk - 7.4%, about 4.2 minutes of the hour - is walked along a lake bed. The player traverses it at 2.0000 m/s in state WALK at full HP and full stamina, with no swim, no wade band, no breath clock and no drowning; a screenshot from that point is a uniformly black-green frame of water volume. Nothing in the instrument suite asks the question: scale-audit.mjs has a TIDEWAY-INVERSION check that measures water depth on exactly one of the ten legs and none on the other nine.
gaps.why_it_matters: The 56.574-minute crossing that every density figure in the corpus is denominated in is measured along a route that stops being walkable the moment RI-WLD10's depth bands land - 502 m at the declared swim speed of 1.1 m/s is 7.6 minutes underwater against a 40-60 second breath clock - so the traversal minute is resting on water having no effect, and a player walking the main road today sees a black screen for four minutes.
